missionPremise: Eleven live polygons in Elgin's Bastrop-side zoning layer carry Zone_Code='S-P', a real Elgin district this repo's codeDomainMap never included (established by CTX-ELGIN 2026-09-09 and independently re-verified live by CTX-ZONESCOPE the same day). Nine of the eleven geometrically cover ten named Bastrop parcels; three of those ten (14457, 12830, 60891) carry no real zoning_district anywhere else, so under the concurrently-built hauska-factory per-parcel write gate they were structurally eligible for a `refused` layer-gap cell -- asserting no zoning coverage on land that is in fact zoned. Source: this dispatch, CTX-ELGIN's and CTX-ZONESCOPE's closes, CTX-PARCELGATE's part2 close (which withheld Bastrop's ceiling specifically pending this lane).
completionPredicate: Done when: (1) S-P's meaning is established from Elgin's own material rather than guessed, and a decision -- map it honestly or declare no honest equivalent -- is made and justified; (2) if no honest equivalent, S-P is staged under its own identity in codeDomainMap, scoped to whichever of the two Elgin registry entries actually carry it; (3) the affected layer is re-staged live, dry-run then apply, with the untouched partition proven unchanged; (4) per-county residue is re-measured with CTX-STAGE2's counting rule verbatim and reported as measured, not as expected; (5) all ten named parcels are confirmed by id, with the three previously-unresolved ones specifically called out; (6) a falsifier on an untouched city still returns non-zero. All six are met below.

spFinding.whatSPIs: "Special Permit" per Elgin_Zoning FeatureServer/0's own service-level description field (attributed to "1. The City of Elgin" in its copyrightText), quoted verbatim: 'Zoning Codes and Descriptions: R-1 Single Family, R-2 Single Family & Duplex, R-3 Single Family, Duplex & Mobile Home, A Multiple Family, C-1 Neighborhood Shopping District, C-2 General Commercial District, C-3 Highway Commercial District, I General Industrial District, S-P Special Permit'. Independently, each of the 11 live S-P features' own per-feature 'Zoning' attribute reads 'Specific Use' (queried live: https://services3.arcgis.com/wdTkTU0MdZbNBEZy/arcgis/rest/services/Elgin_Zoning/FeatureServer/0/query?where=Zone_Code=%27S-P%27). Both descriptions point at the same real-world mechanism: a Specific Use Permit / special-permit grant, corroborated by Elgin's own Planning & Development process (city council review of individual SUP applications, e.g. its own 'SUP 700 Bull Run' agenda item) -- a floating, parcel-specific designation, not a base zoning district.
spFinding.sourceCaveat: A general WebSearch's own synthesized answer, when first asked 'what does S-P mean in Elgin zoning', claimed S-P stood for 'Neighborhood Shopping District'. This was checked against and contradicted by the primary source (the FeatureServer's own domain description, which attributes 'Neighborhood Shopping District' to C-1, not S-P) and discarded, per DEV_PROCESS 3.2a's standard that a correction/claim needs a quoted primary source, not a search-engine paraphrase.
spFinding.noHonestEquivalentDecision: No honest equivalent exists among this program's 8 mapped Elgin base districts (R-1..R-4, C-1..C-3, I). property-reasoning/district-code-section-map.ts's pre-existing ELGIN_TX_MAP (written by an earlier, unrelated lane) already documents that these 8 are exactly the districts established in Elgin Code of Ordinances Chapter 46 Sec. 46-203, each with its own dedicated 'Area regulations' and 'Uses permitted' ordinance sections. A Specific Use Permit does not carry any base district's fixed dimensional/use standards -- its conditions are set individually per grant. Mapping S-P into any of the 8 (e.g. into a spatially-plausible C-1 or R-3 neighbour) would assert that parcel is bound by that district's actual requirements, which is false. Decision: stage S-P under its own identity, 'S-P': 'S-P', matching this program's existing identity-mapping convention (R-1->R-1, etc.), rather than forcing a neighbour.

residuePerCounty.countingRule: CTX-STAGE2's rule verbatim: denom_incity = COUNT(DISTINCT prop_id) from landing_parcel_jurisdiction WHERE city_name='Elgin' AND place_fips='23044' AND disposition='in-city' AND county_fips=C AND prop_id NOT IN ('','0'). denom_with_geom = per-parcel EXISTS aggregation against txgio_parcel geom IS NOT NULL (never a flat join -- txgio_parcel carries multiple rows per prop_id, 48021: 74,729 rows vs 62,257 distinct). matched_count = per-parcel EXISTS aggregation of ST_Contains(ST_SetSRID(ST_GeomFromGeoJSON(z.geometry::text),4326), ST_PointOnSurface(p.geom)) against tx_zoning_district_staging rows with layer_role='base', is_overlay=false, city_key IN ('elgin-tx','elgin-tx-travis'). residue_unmatched = denom_with_geom - matched_count. Run live, restricted by city_key and a numeric-bbox pre-filter on both tables, statement_timeout=45000.

A search engine's synthesized answer to 'what does zoning code X mean' can be wrong even when it cites real district names from the correct city -- it attributed S-P to 'Neighborhood Shopping District' (actually C-1's definition). Always verify a code's meaning against the primary source (here: the live FeatureServer's own domain description and per-feature attribute, both sourced from the City itself) before trusting a search summary, per DEV_PROCESS 3.2a.

A boolean-flag CTE (SELECT EXISTS(...) AS col FROM ...) computing two EXISTS checks per row ran far slower (60s+ timeout) than two separate WHERE-EXISTS-filtered CTEs computing the same two counts independently (each under 45s) against the identical join, same bbox pre-filter, same table. Prefer the WHERE-EXISTS-as-semi-join shape over a SELECT-EXISTS-as-column shape for per-row correlated existence checks against a spatial join in this store -- the planner appears to lose the ability to short-circuit efficiently in the latter form.
